final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed and reframed the same record. That reframing is substantively reasonable in one respect: it correctly distinguishes aggregate launch readiness from compliance with the model-card disclosure predicate. But that interpretation does not close the original audit gap. The policy text is explicit that certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. The admissible record still shows a current subgroup regression, while also showing no attached reviewed mitigation, no owner-approved risk acceptance, and no current certification packet or model-card text proving the required disclosure exists. That means the present record supports general readiness, but not a compliant certification determination on documentation grounds. A caveated defense of what would be needed is not the same as evidence that the predicate has been satisfied now.
remaining_concerns: Policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation.
The admissible evidence shows a current public benefits eligibility regression below the warning threshold.
There is still no admissible evidence that the current certification record or model-card documentation actually includes the required disclosure of the subgroup weakness.
There is still no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation covering the subgroup regression.
Prior family approval remains stale context because it predates the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch.
The release-thread monitoring comment remains informal and does not satisfy the policy requirement for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
